options.B: To list the personal home addresses of study participants
options.C: To explain what each numerical code stands for in the study
options.D: To record the daily vital signs of hospital patients

explanation: Think of a codebook as your translation key. It reminds you what specific numbers (like 1 for Male and 2 for Female) actually represent.

question: What is the primary focus of a midwife's professional practice?

options.A: Diagnosing and treating chronic non-communicable diseases
options.B: Managing complex surgical procedures in tertiary hospitals
options.C: Providing care during pregnancy, labor, and the postpartum period
options.D: Administering pediatric vaccinations exclusively

explanation: Midwives specialize in supporting women through pregnancy, childbirth, and the postnatal stage. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h1)

question: Why might two patients given the exact same dose of a drug experience completely different effects?

options.A: Manufacturers change drug potencies randomly every single day
options.B: Patients always take their prescribed drugs at different times
options.C: Individual biological and environmental factors alter drug disposition
options.D: Hospital pharmacies always dispense different medication strengths

explanation: You'll see this a lot in the wards! Every patient has unique factors like age, diet, and organ function that change how their body handles medications. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h1)

question: Which of these shows direct clinical competence during a nurse's evaluation?

options.A: The total number of personal phone calls made on duty
options.B: How well the nurse gets along with the hospital director
options.C: Correct medication administration technique
options.D: Whether the nurse wears fashionable shoes to work

explanation: Clinical competence is all about the actual nursing care you give. Getting your drug calculations and administration spot-on is a classic example!

question: Why must clinic staff record refrigerator temperatures at least twice every single day?

options.A: To calculate the exact electricity bill for the vaccine unit
options.B: To catch and correct temperature excursions before vaccines spoil
options.C: To make sure the electric fan spins at maximum speed
options.D: To fulfill government paperwork requirements with no real benefit

explanation: Routine checks allow nurses to spot equipment failures early and move vaccines to safety before they are ruined. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h4)

question: What routine test is done on a pregnant woman's urine during antenatal visits?

options.A: Thyroid hormone titers
options.B: Serum electrolyte balance
options.C: Liver enzyme concentrations
options.D: Protein and glucose levels

explanation: Correct! Checking urine helps us catch protein (a sign of pre-eclampsia) or glucose (a sign of gestational diabetes) early.

question: An angry nursing student wants to yell at a strict clinical instructor, but instead channels that energy into scrubbing the skill lab for hours. What defense mechanism is this?

options.A: Sublimation
options.B: Projection
options.C: Regression
options.D: Denial

explanation: That is sublimation! It is taking raw, unacceptable aggression and turning it into something super productive and socially acceptable. Cleaning counts as a win!

question: Why is it so important to build quick rapport with a patient right at the start of an interview?

options.A: It prevents the patient from asking any difficult questions
options.B: It shortens the total time needed for the physical exam
options.C: It guarantees the patient will follow all medication orders
options.D: It lowers patient anxiety and encourages honest sharing

explanation: Exactly! When patients feel safe and respected by you, they relax and open up about what is truly bothering them.

question: Which surfaces in a patient's room need cleaning and disinfecting the most often?

options.A: The outer walls of the hospital storage cupboard
options.B: High ceilings and ceiling fan blades
options.C: High-touch surfaces like bed rails and door handles
options.D: The lower baseboards near the floor corners

explanation: You're right! Bed rails and door handles are touched constantly by hands, so they collect germs the fastest.

question: What is the first step a nurse should take when interpreting any clinical bar chart?

options.A: Ignore the numbers and look only at colors
options.B: Redraw the chart on a blank sheet
options.C: Calculate the exact average of all bars
options.D: Read the chart title and axis labels

explanation: Reading the title and labels ensures you understand what variables and units of measurement the chart represents. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h5)

question: Which group of medications is usually prescribed first for the long-term management of anxiety disorders?

options.A: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs)
options.B: Short-acting skeletal muscle relaxants
options.C: Intravenous corticosteroid therapies
options.D: First-generation antipsychotic medications

explanation: You got it! SSRIs are the go-to choice for long-term anxiety care because they work well and have a safer side-effect profile.

question: Which of the following structures is found inside the cranial cavity?

options.A: Lungs
options.B: Spinal cord
options.C: Brain
options.D: Heart

explanation: The cranial cavity is formed by the skull bones and specifically houses the brain. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why is a functional assessment necessary when caring for someone with a physical disability?

options.A: To prove that the patient is unable to walk
options.B: To diagnose the original cause of the injury
options.C: To determine the financial cost of hospital equipment
options.D: To match nursing interventions with the patient's actual capabilities

explanation: Assessing what a patient can still do prevents nurses from doing tasks the patient is fully capable of managing themselves. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way for a community to prevent parasitic diseases?

options.A: Promoting open defecation near residential water sources
options.B: Advocating for safe sewage disposal infrastructure
options.C: Distributing protective footwear in farming communities
options.D: Encouraging regular handwashing with soap and clean water

explanation: Spot on! Open defecation near water supplies spreads disease rather than stopping it. Handwashing, good sewage systems, and shoes are brilliant preventative steps.

question: Why is keeping accurate and timely nursing notes so important in peri-operative care?

options.A: It allows the patient to perform their own dressing changes.
options.B: It provides a clear legal record of the care provided.
options.C: It replaces the need for verbal handovers between shifts.
options.D: It guarantees that the hospital receives full financial grants.

explanation: Good medical records act as legal proof in court, showing that you delivered safe, standard care at the right time.

question: Which ethical principle guides a nurse's duty to act in the best interest of their psychiatric patient?

options.A: Veracity
options.B: Beneficence
options.C: Paternalism
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Beneficence is all about doing good and taking positive actions to care for and protect your patients. It's at the heart of nursing ethics!

question: Why is it smart for a nurse to involve religious leaders and local heads in a community health plan?

options.A: To dispense prescription antibiotics to villagers
options.B: To gain community buy-in and policy support
options.C: To diagnose complex medical surgical conditions
options.D: To audit hospital financial expenditure records

explanation: Spot on! Local leaders have great influence over the people, so having their backing helps the community welcome new health programs.

question: What is the leading chronic health condition that results in lower limb amputation?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Chronic bronchitis
options.C: Essential hypertension
options.D: Diabetes mellitus

explanation: Diabetes damages blood vessels and nerves over time, making wounds hard to heal and often leading to tissue death. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h1)

question: Which research design is best for answering 'Why or how does this event happen?'

options.A: Explanatory design
options.B: Descriptive design
options.C: Historical design
options.D: Exploratory design

explanation: Brilliant! Explanatory research is built specifically to uncover the 'why' and 'how' behind health events.

question: What does reproductive health truly mean according to the World Health Organization (WHO)?

options.A: A woman's physical capability to carry a pregnancy to full term safely
options.B: The total absence of any bacteria or viruses in the pelvic organs
options.C: The biological ability to conceive and bear children without medical help
options.D: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters

explanation: Think of reproductive health as more than just working body parts. The WHO looks at the whole person—physical, mental, and social well-being together!

question: What does 'patient autonomy' mean in reproductive healthcare?

options.A: The requirement that family elders approve all medical procedures
options.B: The right of the individual to make self-determining choices about their body
options.C: The legal authority of the healthcare provider to choose the best treatment
options.D: The financial independence of the hospital from government oversight

explanation: Autonomy simply means it is the patient's body and their choice. Every individual has the right to decide what happens to their own medical care.

question: How is pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) affecting the Fallopian tubes primarily treated in a stable patient?

options.A: Continuous peritoneal dialysis
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Immediate emergency surgery
options.D: Radiation therapy

explanation: You're crushing it. Because PID is an infection, the frontline treatment is medical—hitting it hard with the right antibiotics to clear the bacteria.

question: A hospital management wants to check if nurses are keeping proper wound care records. What should they do?

options.A: Increasing the number of night shifts for junior nurses
options.B: Transferring patients with wounds to a different facility
options.C: Organizing a social party for all the nursing staff
options.D: Conducting a nursing audit of surgical ward case notes

explanation: Exactly! Reviewing actual clinical charts through an audit gives clear proof of how well wound care is being documented and performed.

question: Why is logistics considered the real backbone of emergency food aid?

options.A: Transporting and delivering food safely to disaster zones requires complex coordination.
options.B: It replaces the need for medical screenings in refugee camps.
options.C: Logistics workers are legally required to cook every meal served to victims.
options.D: Transportation companies pay for all international relief funds.

explanation: Having food is one thing; getting thousands of tons of it across broken bridges and conflict zones to starving people is the real challenge!

question: A patient with terrible watery diarrhea has raw, red skin around their bottom. What is the best immediate nursing care?

options.A: Apply a drying powder to absorb moisture and stop wiping
options.B: Scrub the irritated skin firmly with soap and a rough cloth
options.C: Leave the skin exposed to room air without any protection
options.D: Clean the area gently, dry it, and apply a barrier cream

explanation: You got it! Liquid stool is harsh on the skin. Clean gently and use a good barrier cream to protect raw areas from irritation.

question: A mother brings her toddler to the clinic with signs of malnutrition, mentioning the child only eats corn pap daily. What is this a classic sign of?

options.A: Overconsumption of high-protein energy foods
options.B: Monotonous diet leading to hidden hunger and malnutrition
options.C: A healthy traditional weaning practice for infants
options.D: An allergic reaction to processed maize products

explanation: Spot on! Relying on just one carb source without adding proteins or veggies will quickly lead to serious nutrient shortages.

question: You notice a crying baby's front soft spot looks a bit bulging. What is your best first step as a nurse?

options.A: Document the finding as severe hydrocephalus immediately
options.B: Apply firm pressure to flatten the fontanelle back down
options.C: Prepare an immediate referral for suspected increased intracranial pressure
options.D: Soothe the infant, place them upright, and reassess when quiet

explanation: Brilliant! Always calm the baby first so you can get a true, reliable reading instead of a false alarm.

question: Why are antibiotics often started right away before lab results are even back?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of laboratory diagnostic supplies
options.B: To completely eliminate the need for any follow-up testing
options.C: To cure viral infections like herpes simplex immediately
options.D: To stop the infection from spreading upward into the reproductive tract

explanation: Starting treatment fast prevents the infection from traveling up into the uterus and fallopian tubes, avoiding bigger problems later.

question: Why do midwives and doctors check a baby's fontanelles and sutures during labour?

options.A: To estimate the exact gestational age of the pregnancy
options.B: To measure the exact weight of the foetus before delivery
options.C: To figure out the position and attitude of the baby's head
options.D: To check if the baby's brain is developing normally in utero

explanation: By feeling these soft spots and lines, you can map out which way the baby's head is facing and how well it is flexing to come down.

question: Why do we routinely check a laboring mother's blood pressure?

options.A: To estimate the exact birth weight of the infant
options.B: To detect signs of pre-eclampsia or hemorrhage
options.C: To measure the strength of uterine contractions
options.D: To check how fast the baby's heart is beating

explanation: Spotting dangerous BP spikes (hello, pre-eclampsia!) or sudden drops (bleeding) early lets us protect both mum and baby right away.

question: What is a major sign that a coping behavior is maladaptive rather than helpful?

options.A: It always improves personal relationships
options.B: It appears only once in a person's life
options.C: It is rigid and impairs daily functioning
options.D: It easily resolves without any outside help

explanation: Maladaptive habits are stuck on repeat. Instead of helping you solve a problem, they cause rigid roadblocks that make daily life and relationships harder.

question: How can a nurse best check a baby's skin for a yellow tint during a physical exam?

options.A: Gently pressing the skin over a bony prominence to blanch it
options.B: Pinching a fold of skin on the baby's arm to test elasticity
options.C: Observing the baby inside a dark room using a standard flashlight
options.D: Shining a blue phototherapy light directly onto the infant's abdomen

explanation: Pressing gently over a bone clears the surface blood for a second, making the underlying yellow bilirubin tint much easier to spot. Simple and effective bedside nursing!

question: The human body is primarily divided into which two main structural regions?

options.A: Superior and inferior regions
options.B: Dorsal and ventral cavities
options.C: Axial and appendicular regions
options.D: Anterior and posterior regions

explanation: The body is split into the main central axis and the attached limbs, known respectively as the axial and appendicular regions. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is strong social participation so helpful during a community health crisis?

options.A: Government officials will visit the town more often
options.B: Patients will no longer need to visit physical clinics
options.C: It automatically lowers the cost of imported medicines
options.D: Neighbors are more likely to cooperate and help each other

explanation: Exactly! When people trust and talk to each other, it's much easier to mobilize support and look out for vulnerable ones during emergencies.

question: If a community health nurse notices that immunization rates remain low despite running a vaccination campaign, what should be done next?

options.A: Investigate the barriers causing the low uptake and adjust the strategy
options.B: Report the village to the police for failing to cooperate
options.C: Pretend the campaign was a success and submit fabricated data reports
options.D: Assume the community does not care about health and stop all programs

explanation: Evaluation is an ongoing feedback loop; when targets are missed, nurses must analyze the root causes and modify their approach. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which screening tool is best for catching lung cancer early in high-risk people who don't have symptoms yet?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain
options.B: Standard routine sputum culture
options.C: Pulmonary spirometry test
options.D: Low-dose computed tomography scan

explanation: You've got this! A low-dose CT scan captures clear images of the lungs using very low radiation, making it the gold standard for high-risk screening.

question: What is the core focus of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) when managing chronic health conditions?

options.A: Changing unhelpful thought patterns and building practical coping skills
options.B: Using high doses of medication to alter brain chemistry permanently
options.C: Healing past childhood trauma unrelated to the current illness
options.D: Physically strengthening damaged muscle fibers through exercise

explanation: CBT is all about spotting negative thoughts and swapping them for healthy coping habits to make everyday life a little easier.

question: What is the main reason burn shock happens within the first 24 hours of a severe burn?

options.A: Complete cessation of red blood cell production in the bone marrow
options.B: Sudden slowing of the heart rate due to vagal nerve stimulation
options.C: Massive fluid shift from blood vessels into body tissues
options.D: Rapid drop in core body temperature from environmental exposure

explanation: Right after a big burn, leaky blood vessels let plasma rush out into the tissues. This sudden fluid loss causes burn shock, which is why aggressive fluid replacement is priority number one!

question: Which breathing problem is paragonimiasis most often mistaken for in the clinic?

options.A: Chronic bronchitis
options.B: Asthma exacerbation
options.C: Pulmonary tuberculosis
options.D: Bacterial pneumonia

explanation: Spot on! Because both conditions cause a long-lasting cough and blood-tinged sputum, doctors and nurses often suspect TB first until tests prove otherwise.

question: What is the main difference between endocrine and exocrine glands?

options.A: Endocrine glands lack ducts and release hormones directly into the blood
options.B: Exocrine glands possess a rich network of fenestrated capillaries
options.C: Endocrine glands secrete substances exclusively onto the skin surface
options.D: Exocrine glands produce chemical messengers while endocrine glands do not

explanation: Think of endocrine glands as ductless delivery systems! Because they don't have tubes (ducts), they dump their hormones straight into the bloodstream to travel round the body. You've got this!

question: Which bloodborne infections are most commonly spread through accidental needlestick injuries from poorly managed waste?

options.A: Rhinovirus and Influenza virus
options.B: Plasmodium falciparum and Trypanosoma
options.C: Rabies virus and Ebola virus
options.D: Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV

explanation: Correct! Used sharps carry blood and body fluids that frequently harbor these specific bloodborne viruses. Safety first on the ward!

question: What does 'organisational culture' mean in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: The daily shift schedule assigned by the head nurse
options.B: The physical building layout and available medical equipment
options.C: The written disciplinary policies enforced by human resources
options.D: The shared values and unspoken rules that guide staff behaviour

explanation: Spot on! Culture is all about the invisible norms, habits, and attitudes that shape how work actually gets done on the ward every day.

question: What yummy nickname is often given to old, dark blood-filled cysts found on the ovaries in endometriosis?

options.A: Chocolate cysts
options.B: Serous cystadenomas
options.C: Dermoid tumors
options.D: Fibroid nodules

explanation: They are called 'chocolate cysts' because the old, trapped menstrual blood inside turns dark brown and thick, looking a bit like melted chocolate!

question: You're teaching a patient how to get complete protein from plant sources. Which local food combination should you recommend?

options.A: Yam and palm oil
options.B: Beans and maize
options.C: Cassava and water
options.D: Plantain and salt

explanation: Brilliant! Pairing legumes like beans with a cereal like maize matches up their amino acids to give you a complete, high-quality protein.

question: What is the correct medical term for painful sexual intercourse often reported in endometriosis?

options.A: Dysmenorrhea
options.B: Dysuria
options.C: Dyschezia
options.D: Dyspareunia

explanation: Dyspareunia is the clinical word for pain during or after sex. It happens when pelvic lesions get bumped or stretched.

question: Which payment setup best promotes true equity in a health system?

options.A: Progressive prepayment systems where wealthier individuals contribute more to fund care for everyone
options.B: Relying entirely on patient donations collected inside hospital waiting rooms
options.C: Strict out-of-pocket user fees charged at the hospital door for every single service
options.D: Flat-rate private insurance premiums that cost the same for low- and high-income earners

explanation: When those who earn more chip in a bit extra, it helps protect and cover those who have less. That's true fairness!

question: Which of these is NOT an ethical responsibility of a nurse in a geriatric home?

options.A: Maintaining strict medical confidentiality
options.B: Ignoring resident complaints to save time
options.C: Protecting vulnerable adults from abuse
options.D: Respecting the personal autonomy of the resident

explanation: Ignoring a resident's complaints breaks professional ethics and patient trust. A great nurse always listens and takes action!

question: What is the primary function of a computer?

options.A: Manipulating and processing data
options.B: Storing physical hospital records
options.C: Generating electrical power
options.D: Replacing human clinical judgment

explanation: A computer is fundamentally designed to accept, store, and process raw data into usable information. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h1)

question: What does the 'structure' component of the Donabedian model refer to?

options.A: The steps taken to administer an injection
options.B: The final recovery rate of the patient
options.C: The hospital environment, staff, and equipment
options.D: The financial profit of the clinic

explanation: Easy peasy! In the Donabedian model, 'structure' is the foundation—it's about the tools, buildings, and skilled staff we have available to do our work.

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended way to handle patient resistance?

options.A: Exploring the underlying emotional fears behind the refusal
options.B: Confronting the patient with strict authority and harsh demands
options.C: Using motivational interviewing to find common ground
options.D: Offering safe choices to give the patient back some control

explanation: Spot on! Coming down hard with bossy commands only makes a patient push back harder. Empathy and choices work way better than strict orders.

question: Why must a nurse avoid using their thumb when feeling a patient's pulse?

options.A: The thumb lacks the nerve endings needed to feel heart rhythms
options.B: The thumb is too weak to press firmly against a major artery
options.C: Using the thumb violates strict hospital infection control rules
options.D: The thumb has its own pulse that can be mistaken for the patient's

explanation: The thumb contains a prominent pulse of its own, which can cause the nurse to count their own heartbeat instead of the patient's. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h4)

question: What does the term 'cachexia' mean in advanced illness?

options.A: A sudden increase in daily appetite
options.B: Complete blockage of the large intestine
options.C: An infection caused by poor dental hygiene
options.D: Severe muscle wasting and weight loss

explanation: You've got this! Cachexia is a whole-body wasting condition caused by disease inflammation, not just because the person isn't eating enough food.

question: What is the primary building block used to present qualitative research findings?

options.A: Zero-baseline bar charts
options.B: Statistical p-values and correlations
options.C: Themes and direct participant quotes
options.D: Decimal-aligned numeric tables

explanation: Qualitative research focuses on human experiences, which are presented through organized themes and verbatim quotes rather than numbers. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the main difference between microvascular and macrovascular complications in diabetes?

options.A: Microvascular conditions involve low blood sugar, while macrovascular conditions involve high blood sugar
options.B: Macrovascular damage is reversible with diet, whereas microvascular damage requires surgery
options.C: Microvascular affects tiny vessels in the eyes, kidneys, and nerves, while macrovascular affects large vessels like the heart and brain
options.D: Microvascular complications only occur in Type 1 while macrovascular only occur in Type 2

explanation: 'Micro' means tiny (eyes, kidneys, nerves), and 'macro' means large (heart, brain). Long-term high sugar hurts both sizes of blood vessels in different ways!

question: What part of the fibrous tunic is completely clear to let light pass into the eye?

options.A: Cornea
options.B: Retina
options.C: Sclera
options.D: Choroid

explanation: The cornea is the transparent front window of the eye that bends and admits light. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h2)

question: Which gland gets a direct emergency signal from nerves during stress?

options.A: Adrenal medulla
options.B: Parathyroid gland
options.C: Anterior pituitary
options.D: Thyroid gland

explanation: When you get a sudden fright, the nervous system instantly triggers the adrenal medulla to pump out adrenaline for that fight-or-flight burst.

question: Why does visiting a patient's home often reveal health details that a clinic visit misses?

options.A: Clinic doctors lack the training to ask patients about their daily habits.
options.B: Hospital staff deliberately hide dietary information from visiting relatives.
options.C: Patients cannot remember their medical history when they leave their house.
options.D: Seeing the home environment uncovers hidden barriers to proper self-care.

explanation: You got it! Walking into their space lets you spot real-life challenges—like a lack of food or unsafe furniture—that they might forget to mention at the clinic.

question: Why is it hard to use raw numbers straight from a patient audit without descriptive statistics?

options.A: They are illegal to share within a hospital ward
options.B: They always contain mathematical calculation errors
options.C: They only apply to laboratory experiments
options.D: They are too overwhelming to spot patterns without organization

explanation: Think of raw data as a scattered mess of puzzle pieces. Without organizing them first, it's nearly impossible to spot trends or make sense of what's happening on the ward!

question: What is the main purpose of using the teach-back method?

options.A: To fulfill strict insurance billing rules
options.B: To confirm whether the patient truly understands the instructions
options.C: To give the nurse a break from talking
options.D: To test the patient's long-term memory capacity

explanation: Correct! Asking them to explain it back in their own words is the best way to make sure they got the right message.

question: What kind of practical help can faith-based communities offer to people with physical disabilities?

options.A: Official legal representation in medical malpractice lawsuits
options.B: Mandatory hospital accreditation and safety inspections
options.C: Volunteer networks and accessible transportation assistance
options.D: Advanced surgical interventions and prescription drug manufacturing

explanation: Religious and faith groups often step up with volunteers to help members with rides, meals, and companionship when moving around is tough.

question: How do scientists use bacteria like E. coli in modern recombinant DNA technology?

options.A: To destroy unwanted chemical impurities inside synthetic drug vials
options.B: To serve as natural painkillers harvested during fermentation
options.C: To extract raw mineral salts directly from underground rock beds
options.D: To act as biological factories that produce human proteins like insulin

explanation: By putting human genes into bacteria, scientists turn them into tiny biological factories that safely pump out human proteins like insulin.

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team essential in palliative symptom management?

options.A: Doctors are not allowed to speak directly with family members
options.B: Complex physical and emotional symptoms require varied professional expertise
options.C: Hospital regulations state that five nurses must see every patient
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to perform any physical assessments

explanation: No single discipline can address every physical, psychological, and spiritual need of a dying patient. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h8)

question: What is a common cause of accidental poisoning among young children in many Nigerian households?

options.A: Commercial industrial solvents kept in clinical labs
options.B: Prescription antihypertensive tablets left on tables
options.C: Imported cosmetics applied to the skin
options.D: Kerosene stored in empty beverage bottles

explanation: Storing hazardous fuel in familiar soft drink containers easily misleads thirsty children, leading to accidental ingestion and severe aspiration pneumonia. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h3)

question: What is one major perk of condoms over hormonal birth control pills?

options.A: Condoms require no action at the time of intercourse
options.B: Condoms cause permanent changes in fertility
options.C: Condoms have a much higher real-world perfection rate
options.D: Condoms offer protection against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: You got it! While pills are great for preventing pregnancy, only barrier methods like condoms protect against STIs too.

question: In which week of enteric fever is a blood culture most likely to give a positive result?

options.A: Fifth week
options.B: Sixth week
options.C: Third week
options.D: First week

explanation: Spot on! The bacteria is highest in the bloodstream right at the start of the illness, making the first week ideal for a blood culture.

question: Which of these is a key nursing duty before a client has a neurological scan?

options.A: Applying a plaster cast to keep the head steady
options.B: Deciding the exact dose of contrast dye
options.C: Checking consent, allergies, and looking out for metal
options.D: Reading and interpreting the X-ray films yourself

explanation: Nurses are safety champions! We verify consent, screen for allergies, and check for metal before tests.

question: Why do babies with sickle cell anaemia usually look completely healthy at birth?

options.A: The bone marrow does not produce red blood cells until the age of one
options.B: Infant blood vessels are too wide for blockages to possibly form
options.C: The mother's immune system filters out all the abnormal blood cells
options.D: High levels of fetal haemoglobin protect the red blood cells temporarily

explanation: Fetal haemoglobin (HbF) is tough and resists sickling. It's only when HbF starts dropping after birth that symptoms begin to show up.

question: What is a major advantage of Rapid Diagnostic Tests in primary health care?

options.A: They provide quick results with minimal equipment
options.B: They eliminate the need for clinical history taking
options.C: They are completely free to manufacture worldwide
options.D: They never give false results

explanation: RDTs are designed to give fast answers at the bedside or in remote clinics without needing heavy laboratory machinery. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h4)

question: In clinical nursing, how do we truly know how much pain a patient is in?

options.A: Pain only exists if visible tissue damage is present.
options.B: Pain is whatever the experiencing patient says it is.
options.C: Pain is a psychological illusion created by anxiety.
options.D: Pain can be accurately measured solely by high blood pressure.

explanation: Remember this golden rule of nursing: pain is subjective. If the patient says it hurts, it hurts! Always trust and validate your patient's report.

question: During which phase of the nurse-patient relationship do you first build trust and set professional boundaries?

options.A: The termination phase
options.B: The working phase
options.C: The pre-interaction phase
options.D: The orientation phase

explanation: The orientation phase is your official 'meet and greet' where you introduce yourself, set ground rules, explain your roles, and start building that vital therapeutic trust.

question: Which of the following is NOT measured by GDP or GNP?

options.A: Total market value of goods
options.B: Total income generated by businesses
options.C: Overall population health and happiness
options.D: Monetary value of services rendered

explanation: GDP and GNP only measure money and production. They don't capture human well-being, happiness, or social health directly.

question: What effect does progesterone have on the gallbladder during pregnancy?

options.A: It causes sluggish emptying and bile stasis
options.B: It stops the liver from producing cholesterol
options.C: It causes the gallbladder to shrink significantly
options.D: It speeds up the release of concentrated bile

explanation: Just like the gut, the gallbladder muscles relax too. This makes it empty slower, leaving bile sitting inside longer (stasis).

question: Why does blood pressure fall in early and mid-pregnancy even though blood volume is rising?

options.A: Kidneys excrete all excess fluid immediately
options.B: The heart pumps with much less force
options.C: Blood vessels constrict to push blood to the lungs
options.D: Progesterone reduces systemic vascular resistance

explanation: Brilliant! Progesterone relaxes blood vessel walls so they widen, which naturally lowers resistance and blood pressure.

question: A confused patient arrives at the emergency department with suspected drug ingestion. What quick bedside check must a nurse perform right away?

options.A: Checking blood glucose level
options.B: Measuring abdominal girth
options.C: Testing deep tendon reflexes
options.D: Checking visual acuity

explanation: Always rule out low blood sugar first! Severe hypoglycemia can look identical to a drug overdose, so a quick finger-prick blood glucose check is a nursing essential.

question: When is it most appropriate to give a patient an antitussive (cough suppressant)?

options.A: For a dry, hacking cough that prevents sleep
options.B: For treating a bacterial sinus infection
options.C: For clearing thick, green mucus from the lungs
options.D: For lowering a high fever during the flu

explanation: Antitussives are best saved for those exhausting, dry coughs that keep patients awake all night. Let's help them sleep!

question: What is the main job of an Automated External Defibrillator (AED)?

options.A: Monitor continuous blood oxygen saturation levels in the field
options.B: Infuse intravenous fluids to maintain systemic blood pressure
options.C: Deliver an electrical shock to restart a chaotic heart rhythm
options.D: Provide mechanical chest compressions during a cardiac arrest

explanation: You're doing great! An AED is a smart machine that reads the heart's rhythm and gives a quick electrical shock to reset dangerous rhythms like VFib so the heart can beat properly again.

question: What is needed to make community health schemes truly successful in Nigeria?

options.A: Government backing, transparent management, and public education
options.B: Making health insurance compulsory only for the wealthy
options.C: Complete elimination of primary health care centers
options.D: Relying solely on foreign donor grants forever

explanation: For long-term success, we need strong support from institutions, honest handling of funds, and well-informed citizens who understand the benefits.

question: Which body part is mainly affected in a Type I FGM procedure?

options.A: The perineal body
options.B: The vaginal opening
options.C: The clitoris
options.D: The entire labia majora

question: What is most important when creating health education posters for a rural Nigerian community?

options.A: Ensuring every poster costs very little to print
options.B: Writing the text exclusively in advanced medical English
options.C: Featuring foreign medical experts on the cover page
options.D: Using local languages and familiar cultural imagery

explanation: For health messages to stick, people need to see themselves in the pictures and understand the language without struggling. Keep it relatable! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h5)

question: Why must disaster nurses actively watch out for compassion fatigue and practice self-care?

options.A: Patients will lose respect for nurses who show emotion
options.B: Nurses are immune to stress if they work fast enough
options.C: Hospital managers require daily wellness logs from every nurse
options.D: Prolonged exposure to trauma can lead to severe emotional burnout

explanation: So true! Seeing constant suffering wears down even the strongest nurses. Taking care of your own mental health keeps you and your patients safe.

question: What is the main goal of giving post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) right after an accidental needle stick?

options.A: To cure a chronic bacterial skin infection
options.B: To prevent the establishment of a viral infection
options.C: To numb the skin and prevent local tissue scarring
options.D: To relieve muscle spasms around the injury site

explanation: PEP uses quick antiviral meds to stop a virus from taking hold and multiplying after an accidental exposure. Every minute counts!

question: Which of these is NOT a barrier to patient education?

options.A: Quiet and comfortable physical environment
options.B: Severe pain and physical fatigue
options.C: Language and cultural differences
options.D: High anxiety and fear of diagnosis

explanation: Spot on! A quiet, comfortable space actually helps learning happen, whereas pain, anxiety, and language gaps get in the way.

question: Why shouldn't healthcare workers hand-wash contaminated Lassa patient linens in open basins?

options.A: Modern detergents are too expensive for primary clinics
options.B: It risks splashing infectious bodily fluids and spreading the virus
options.C: Washing powder damages the fabric of hospital bedsheets
options.D: Soap destroys the color of standard hospital linen sets

explanation: Washing linen by hand in open spaces creates splashes and mists that can expose staff to dangerous viral particles.

question: What is an organ made of?

options.A: Individual atoms bonded tightly into complex organic molecules
options.B: A collection of identical cells performing the exact same task
options.C: Two or more different types of tissues working together
options.D: Multiple organ systems functioning inside a single body cavity

explanation: Think of an organ like a team! It takes different tissue types working together—like muscle and lining tissues—to get a big job done. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h2)

question: A patient arrives at a local primary health clinic with a deep, bleeding wound and signs of shock. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Prescribe mild herbal tea and send the patient away
options.B: Provide first aid, stabilize the wound, and arrange urgent referral to a hospital
options.C: Tell the patient to walk home and rest quietly in bed
options.D: Wait until the next national health campaign day to treat them

explanation: Severe injuries and shock exceed primary clinic capabilities, requiring immediate stabilization and referral to a higher level of care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h8)

question: A patient with a painful ankle gout flare says even the bedsheet touching the skin is agonizing. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Massage the ankle firmly to increase circulation and numb the area
options.B: Use a bed cradle to keep the linens elevated off the painful ankle
options.C: Encourage the patient to walk around the room to break up the crystals
options.D: Apply a warm heating pad directly to the skin over the joint

explanation: A bed cradle is a simple device that keeps blankets lifted off the foot, giving immediate relief to an extremely tender joint.

question: Why is it so important to tape and secure the NG tube firmly to the patient's nose?

options.A: To stop the stomach from producing normal digestive acids
options.B: To prevent friction and trauma to the nasal mucosa from tube movement
options.C: To make the tube completely invisible from the outside

question: Why does community health nursing place a strong emphasis on health maintenance?

options.A: It completely eliminates all infectious diseases from a population
options.B: It shifts the nurse's job entirely to administrative desk work
options.C: It makes physical examinations completely unnecessary for adults
options.D: It reduces the need for expensive hospital care by stopping illness early

explanation: Focusing on wellness helps catch problems early and keeps people out of hospital beds. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h1)

question: How does proper birth spacing protect a mother's health?

options.A: It gives the mother's body time to recover nutrients and strength
options.B: It eliminates the need for any antenatal checkups
options.C: It completely prevents the onset of gestational diabetes
options.D: It guarantees that the next baby will be born full-term

explanation: Giving the body a break between pregnancies allows nutrient stores to refill, making future pregnancies much safer for mum. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h2)

question: What is a major reason families ask health workers to perform FGM?

options.A: Government laws require a medical certificate for marriage

options.C: Traditional cutters are no longer available in cities
options.D: Doctors charge much lower fees than traditional cutters

question: What is the main goal of gathering public health surveillance data?

options.A: To guide health policy and practical actions
options.B: To increase the cost of medical treatments
options.C: To punish clinics that report too many sick patients
options.D: To fill up hospital filing cabinets with paperwork

explanation: We don't collect health data just to sit on shelves! It's meant to be put to work for planning and stopping diseases in our communities.

question: How can severe stress or trauma in childhood affect a person later in life?

options.A: It has no lasting impact once the individual reaches maturity.
options.B: It only influences physical health rather than psychological well-being.
options.C: It can alter brain development and prime the nervous system to overreact to future stress.
options.D: It guarantees the person will develop panic disorder by early adulthood.
